sentence: This project builds tools that help predict which patients with ankylosing spondylitis are at risk of severe spinal disease, using molecular profiling and biomarkers.
This project studies how the gut balances stem cell division with cell death, and how stretch from food intake makes the gut grow.
This project studies how a chain of linked molecules controls self-renewal in hematopoietic and leukemic stem cells.
This project tests whether a protein in the dentin matrix helps dental pulp stem cells turn into cells that make dentin.
This project studies how antimicrobial-resistant bacteria spread and change genetically across the world, using genomic data from Africa.
This project studies how a signaling pathway in tumor cells helps head and neck cancer resist immune-checkpoint inhibitors.
This project tests how well a digital therapeutic that uses remote substance testing and contingency management treats stimulant use disorder.
This project studies how the mammalian cerebral cortex develops, works and fails to work.
This project runs a shared facility that offers sequencing, proteomics, flow cytometry and mass spectrometry services for cancer research.
This project studies how the kinetochore attaches to DNA and to microtubules of the mitotic spindle so chromosomes are shared between new cells.
This project buys an automated imaging system that scans tissue slides and measures proteins and nucleic acids in them.
This project searches trillions of peptides for rare ones that stick to clumps of huntingtin protein without binding other parts of the cell.
This project runs a facility that makes genetically engineered mice for studying human diseases, especially cancer, using genome editing.
This project provides sequencing technologies that help researchers study how changes in the epigenome affect gene expression in diabetes.
This project offers flow cytometric analysis and cell sorting to measure cellular biomarkers in cancer-related research.
This project offers imaging of tumors in living animals and of tumor tissue slides, using ultrasound, optical and computed tomography imaging.
This project tests how a treatment aimed at a small group of tumor cells that cause metastasis works best for undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
This project looks for biomarkers that tell apart complex inflammatory skin diseases so existing treatments can be better directed.
This project studies how human cells help an abundant protein fold into its correct three-dimensional shape and how cells adapt to stress.
This project studies how osteoclasts, the cells that break down bone, are regulated, since too much of their activity causes excessive bone loss.
